title: Visual Translation Memory (VTM)
description: A TM that preserves the graphic profile of text; (s, t) strings anchored to a certain image region with typographical metadata needed to re-render them faithfully.

vtm_version.description: format version. readers implementing 1.x MUST accept any 1.y document and ignore keys they do not recognize.

generator.description: the 'what' --  i.e., the source of asset (document) production.

source_language.description: asset-level source language. Entries MAY override.

target_language.description: asset-level target language. Entries MAY override.

asset.description: the image the geometry belongs to. required: asset resolution (bbox is uninterpretable otherwise) -- e.g., (10,20,100,30) describes a different region on a 640px thumbnail than on a 4096px original.

sha256.description: optional content hash, so a memory can be tied to an exact asset.

bbox.description: axis-aligned rectangle in px. origin == top-left of the asset; x increases rightward, y increases downward. named keys rather than a 4-tuple: array ordering is the most common source of silent interop bugs in this shape.

polygon.description: optional tighter outline in the same pixel space, for rotated or curved text the bbox over-covers.

rotation.description: baseline rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise positive.

reading_order.description: position in the asset's reading sequence. Matters for multi-region signage where order carries meaning.

style.description: portable typography. this is a subset of what a renderer may know: every key is one a competing implementation can reasonably honor. engine-specific controls belong under an x- extension.

weight.description: e.g. 'normal', 'bold', or a numeric CSS weight as a string.

background.description: what the text sat on. Enables a consumer to erase and re-render, not merely to read.

provenance.description: how much to trust this entry. evidently, a visual TM that reuses a low-confidence pair is worse than one that reuses nothing.

confidence.description: recognition confidence for the src text.

qa_score.description: quality of the rendered tgt, if it was rendered and scored.

glyph_fallback.description: true when the requested face lacked coverage and a substitute was used.

visual.description: fingerprints for matching this entry (asset(1)() against a region of another asset (asset(2)) -- the mechanism that makes a visual TM reusable rather than merely archival.

phash.description: Perceptual hash of the source region crop.

source.description: Text as it appears in the asset.

^x-.description: vendor extension. Readers must ignore x- keys they do not recognize and MUST NOT let their absence change interpretation of the standard keys.
